clips.title: The story
paras: At Ban'ethil Barrow Den, an urgent effort is underway to save the sleeping Druids of the Talon. Corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have overrun the sacred mounds, threatening the druids whose spirits wander the Emerald Dream. Four ritual relics are needed to bring the sleepers safely back to the waking world.

West of Dolanaar, a swarm of corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs has overrun the winding corridors of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Barrow dens are secluded sanctuaries where night elf druids hibernate while their spirits walk the Emerald Dream. A foul taint spreading across Teldrassil has driven these former allies mad. They have desecrated the sanctum, leaving the sleepers unaware that danger threatens their physical bodies.

Athridas Bearmantle needs four sacred relics for the delicate ceremony that can safely awaken the Druids of the Talon. A druid's spirit needs an anchor when returning from the Dream; without one, a sudden awakening can shatter the mind or strand the spirit. The relics lie in chests across the den: the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting. They are the sleepers' only hope before the Gnarlpine butcher or abduct them.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Gnarlpine invaders were seen ravaging the Ban'ethil Barrow Den to the west.
The slumbering druids will be trapped in the Emerald Dream for eternity, unaware of their fate, unless we help. The delicate hibernation ritual cannot be broken without the Relics of Wakening.

Journey to the Den and retrieve the Raven Claw Talisman, Black Feather Quill, Sapphire of Sky, and Rune of Nesting. The druids store them in sacred chests. Return them to me and I will prepare the awakening ritual.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Friend, the kidnapped Druids of the Talon will be forever trapped in the Emerald Dream if we cannot retrieve the Relics of Wakening from the Ban'ethil Barrow Den to the west.
For every minute we delay their fate comes one step closer to eternal doom.

clips.title: Completion
paras: You have succeeded, young adventurer! Well done. And just in time I might add.
